candidate.selection_reason: SQL parameter values -> dialect-aware escaping -> SQL injection protection mechanism
candidate.source_summary: Values parameter passed to SqlString.format function, which can come from user-provided replacements in Sequelize.query() or from query generator conditions
candidate.sink_summary: SQL query execution via Sequelize connector manager after parameter substitution
candidate.guard_summary: SqlString.escape provides dialect-aware escaping for SQL injection protection, but uses false for stringifyObjects parameter which affects object handling
candidate.risk_pattern: Parameterized SQL query construction with dialect-specific escaping, but potential bypass if objects are not properly stringified
enclosing_conditions: values array has elements to replace placeholders
candidate.context_summary: Core SQL formatting function used throughout Sequelize ORM for safe parameter substitution in queries
unresolved_facts: Whether all callers properly validate/sanitize input before passing to SqlString.format
Security impact of stringifyObjects=false parameter in object handling scenarios

target_cwe.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')
target_cwe.description: The product constructs all or part of an LDAP query using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended LDAP query when it is sent to a downstream component. Common in: sql_injection, input_validation.
target_cwe.impact: code execution, data access, data modification
remediation_steps: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements
Implement strict input validation with whitelisting
